source.version: Published conference paper, Proceedings of the 58th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS-58), 2025, printed pages 342-351; URI https://hdl.handle.net/10125/108877
source.title_on_document: Fostering Innovation with Generative AI: A Study on Human-AI Collaborative Ideation and User Anonymity

supplement.where: The paper mentions no supplement or appendix. It links the system code at https://github.com/graasp/graasp-app-collaborative-ideation (p. 2, printed p. 343, Section 3).

paper_design_summary: Twenty-nine Master's students in a course on information system design ideated in groups with AI-deation, an app in which a GPT-3.5 idea editor rewrites every submitted idea for anonymity. The students were randomly divided into a human-only condition and a condition where an AI collaborator posted two ideas per round into the group pool, over three rounds of three minutes. Participants rated every idea for novelty, the two first authors rated every idea for innovation, and the paper also compares AI-generated ideas with participants' ideas.

studies.label: Classroom experiment: AI collaborator vs human-only group ideation

assignment.what_was_assigned: Presence of an AI collaborator (GPT-3.5) that posts two new ideas into the group's idea pool each round, versus human-only ideation. The idea editor was active in both conditions.
assignment.quote: In this experiment, we randomly divided the participants into two conditions. The baseline condition (human-only) involved only participants generating ideas, while the treatment condition ... had the AI collaborator suggesting two new ideas at each round.

arms.name: Humans and AI collaborator
arms.description: Participants ideate in AI-deation; an AI collaborator adds two ideas to the pool at each round; submitted ideas are rewritten by the LLM idea editor.

arms.name: Humans only
arms.description: Participants ideate in AI-deation without the AI collaborator; submitted ideas are still rewritten by the LLM idea editor.

participants.exclusions: 32 students attended the course and 29 consented to the study; the 29 consenting participants are analyzed (13 control, 16 treatment). The paper does not give counts at assignment. Questionnaire analyses use 28 or 29 respondents (t(27), t(28)); 25 answered the open question on the pool of ideas.
participants.who: Master's students in General Management taking a 6-ECTS course on information system design; 9 male, 23 female among the 32 attendees; most not native English speakers.
participants.country: not_stated (authors at University of Neuchâtel and EPFL; the course is at 'our University')
participants.quote: Thirty-two students (9 male, 23 female) attended the course, and 29 consented to the study.
participants.locator: p. 4 (printed p. 345), Section 4; p. 5 (printed p. 346), Section 5

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-3.5 Turbo (OpenAI, gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 per the reference list)
ai_tool.how_used: At the end of each round the AI collaborator is prompted with the problem and the group's ideas to generate a 'disruptive, and out-of-the-box solution' (max 200 characters) that is added to the pool; it suggested two ideas per round in the treatment condition (48 AI ideas in total). In both conditions an LLM idea editor reformulated every submitted idea in a neutral tone to strengthen anonymity. No control prevented participants from using other AI tools such as ChatGPT.

task.description: Group ideation on complex problems tied to the course project on Sustainable Development Goals (example on screenshot: 'How might we motivate people to change their behaviour to improve their health and well-being?'); participants could propose a new idea or build on a shown idea, max 200 characters.
task.duration: Three rounds of three minutes each, in one class session, followed by idea rating and a questionnaire

outcomes.name: Innovation of participants' ideas rated by the two first authors
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two of the authors rated every idea on a five-level innovation scale adapted from Shaer et al. (2024) ('how original and creative the idea is, breaking away from the conventional or existing solutions'); ideas de-identified and shuffled within challenge; initial agreement r < .5, disagreements of 1 or more discussed, final r(350) = .79. Whether raters saw original or reformulated text is not stated.

contrasts.reported: One-sided Mann-Whitney U test (H1: treatment > control): U = 2803, p-value = .8; boxplots in Figure 7. Ideas per arm: 76 participant ideas in treatment, 77 in control (n_units = 76 + 77 from p. 5).

outcomes.name: Novelty of participants' ideas rated by the participants
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: After ideation, participants rated every idea of their group on a 5-point Likert scale for novelty (and usefulness; usefulness results are not reported). Raters are the participants themselves, rating peers' and their own group's ideas.

contrasts.reported: Mann-Whitney U test: U = 3501.5, p-value = .983 ('no evidence to support a significant difference'); boxplots in Figure 6, lower panel.
contrasts.locator: p. 5 (printed p. 346), Section 5.2; p. 6 (printed p. 347), Figure 6

outcomes.name: Number of ideas submitted per participant
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of ideas I_p submitted by each participant; 77 ideas from 13 control participants, 76 from 16 treatment participants.

contrasts.reported: Welch's t-test: t(24.6) = 1.33, p-value = .2; Figure 8 boxplots. Totals: control 13 participants, 77 ideas; treatment 16 participants, 76 ideas.
contrasts.locator: p. 5 (printed p. 346), Section 5; p. 7 (printed p. 348), Section 5.2, Figure 8

outcomes.name: Innovation of AI-generated ideas vs participants' ideas (author ratings)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Same five-level innovation scale rated by two authors as in S1-O1.

contrasts.reported: One-sided Mann-Whitney U test (H1: AI > participants): U = 1629, p-value < .001; Figure 7 upper panel.
contrasts.locator: p. 6 (printed p. 347), Section 5.2; p. 7 (printed p. 348), Figure 7

outcomes.name: Novelty of AI-generated ideas vs participants' ideas (participant ratings)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Participants' 5-point novelty ratings, as in S1-O2.

contrasts.reported: One-sided Mann-Whitney U test (H1: AI > participants): U = 4463, p-value = .012; Figure 6 upper panel.
contrasts.locator: p. 5 (printed p. 346), Section 5.2; p. 6 (printed p. 347), Figure 6

company_involvement.description: No company authors or funders; the tools run on OpenAI's GPT-3.5 Turbo API. Funding: Swissuniversities P8 digital skills program and EPFL Collaborative Research on Science and Society program.

eligibility.reason: Participants were randomly divided between an AI-collaborator condition and a human-only condition, and idea innovation, novelty, and counts are scored on the output, but only 29 people were analyzed (13 control, 16 treatment; p. 5, printed p. 346), well below 50. The control arm also used the LLM idea editor, so the contrast is one AI configuration versus another. The paper's AI-vs-participant idea comparisons are context of the ai_vs_human kind inside the same experiment.

one_line_finding: With 29 students, adding a GPT-3.5 AI collaborator to group ideation did not change the innovation of participants' ideas (Mann-Whitney U = 2803, p = .8), their peer-rated novelty (U = 3501.5, p = .983), or ideas per person (t(24.6) = 1.33, p = .2), although the AI's own ideas rated higher (pp. 5-7, printed pp. 346-348, Figures 6-8).
open_questions: Unit of assignment: the text says participants were randomly divided, but ideation happened in groups that share an idea pool, so assignment may have been by group; the paper gives no group counts per condition.
Design class: the experiment ran in a regular class session of a Master's course; coded field_rct (coursework), but lab_rct is defensible.
Comparison type: both arms used the GPT-3.5 idea editor that rewrote every idea, so the contrast is coded ai_design rather than ai_vs_bau.
Whether the innovation and novelty ratings were made on the original or the LLM-reformulated idea text is not stated.

Unit and n for the Mann-Whitney tests on novelty (individual ratings vs per-idea scores) are not stated; the innovation reliability statistic r(350) implies 352 rated items, which does not match the 201 total ideas.
notes: No means, SDs, or effect sizes are printed; only U statistics, p-values, and boxplots. Mann-Whitney tests treat ideas or ratings as independent observations. Usefulness was rated by participants but not reported. Self-reported outcomes (S-UEQ score 0.2, 13 Likert statements on anonymity and the idea editor, open questions) are not on the output and are not listed.
